author: Bobby Grayson
description:
FILES (4 commits on wf6/pubsub, branched at d7be198): modified Leanactors/Sys.lean, Leanactors/SysProps.lean, Leanactors/Examples/SupervisorLive.lean (three new Effect cases in mboxOf_applyEffect_append), elixir/to_lean.exs, check.sh, Leanactors.lean; new Leanactors/Gen/Feed.lean, Leanactors/Examples/Feed.lean, elixir/src/feed.ex, elixir/src/pubsub.ex, elixir/feed.exs, elixir/test/fixtures/{pubsub.ex,pubsub_root.ex,error_pubsub_topic.ex}, elixir/test/expected/{pubsub.lean,pubsub_root.lean}. Leanactors.lean gains 'import Leanactors.Gen.Feed' and 'import Leanactors.Examples.Feed' at the end; check.sh gains one translate line, one diff -q line and 'elixir elixir/feed.exs | tail -1' after the registry driver.

COUNTS on this branch alone: 13,692 hand-written lines / 30 files / 760 theorems (lines starting with 'theorem '), 398 generated lines / 8 Gen files, 40 fixtures (31 ok, 9 error).

README Status: eight worked examples (add feed); the feed, like the registry, has its property checked but not yet proved (a weaker fact about it is proved: every subscription is to "feed" and never the publisher's). Fixture count 40 (31 ok, 9 error).

README example table row: | Feed | every subscriber has received a prefix of the published sequence | 53,845 |

README Layout rows (after the Registry row):
| `Leanactors/Examples/Feed.lean` | PubSub feed translated from `elixir/src/feed.ex`: a publisher broadcasting `post n` on the topic "feed", two subscribers that subscribe in `init/1` and count posts, one leaving; hand `beh`, `beh_eq_gen`, bounded checker for 'each subscriber has seen a prefix of the published sequence and is owed exactly the rest, in order', two mutants (no unsubscribe, stale number), `subs_feed_only` proved through `SysStep.mem_subs_cases` |
and after the ttl.exs/registry.exs driver rows:
| `elixir/feed.exs` | Driver: a publisher broadcasts three posts over the local PubSub twin, one subscriber leaves, two more posts; states and the subscriber list checked against Lean's `script` |
| `elixir/src/pubsub.ex` | A 44-line local stand-in for `Phoenix.PubSub` (`subscribe/2`, `unsubscribe/2`, `broadcast/3`, `subscribers/2`) so the drivers run without the `phoenix_pubsub` dependency; not translated, it is the transport |
(the `elixir/src/*.ex` row's list of modules gains feed)

README, new paragraph for the model section (next to Maps): 'PubSub. A `Sys` carries `subs : List (String x Pid)`, subscriptions oldest first. `Effect.subscribe q t` appends, `Effect.unsubscribe q t` filters, and `Effect.broadcast t m` is one `deliverAll` of `m` to every subscriber of `t` in subscription order, so a broadcast changes no state and adds one mailbox copy per subscription; a death drops the dead pid s subscriptions. The subscriber pid is explicit because a `Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe` inside `init/1` belongs to the child, whose pid is `fresh` at the parent s spawn site. Topics are strings, resolved by the translator from a literal or a string-valued module attribute; a computed topic is an error.'

NOTES round-6 section bullets for this piece: (1) PubSub is a broadcast effect over a subscription list, not a process: one `deliverAll` in subscription order, `terminate` unsubscribes the dead. (2) The subscriber pid had to be explicit in the effect, which is what makes `init/1` subscriptions expressible at the spawn site; the price is that a root actor that subscribes in `init/1` has no spawn site, which the translator now warns about. (3) `Sys.Grows`/`Sys.Frame` were deliberately not extended: an `unsubscribe` shrinks `subs`, so monotonicity is stated under an explicit no-unsubscribe hypothesis (`Effect.keepsSubs`), and `SysStep.mem_subs_cases` is the induction workhorse. (4) The local `pubsub.ex` twin keeps the repository dependency-free while matching Phoenix s function shapes, including dropping a subscriber on its DOWN.
title: Integrator record for wf6/pubsub: README/NOTES replacement text and the files touched
